paper_metadata.title: High strain rate deformation mechanism of extruded WE43 magnesium alloy at room temperature and 400 °C

evidence.quote: This study investigates the deformation behavior of extruded WE43 magnesium alloy under a strain rate of 1400 s-1 at both room temperature and 400°C.

evidence.quote: the twin distribution map (Fig. 5 i) indicates that the primary twin type is the {10-12} tensile twin, accounting for 5.3%, whereas the fractions of {10-11} compression twins and compound twins are extremely low.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure observation after high speed impact
evidence.quote: LAGBs (2°<θ<10°) account for as much as 72.5%, and the proportion of high-angle grain boundaries (HAGBs) is relatively low and smooth, further confirming that the alloy is in a substructure state characterized by a high dislocation density.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure observation after high speed impact
evidence.quote: In contrast to the RT condition, at 400°C, the alloy does not undergo complete fracture, and the crack width is narrower, indicating that high temperatures enhance the material’s plastic deformation capability.

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure observation after high speed impact

evidence.section: 3.2. Microstructure observation after high speed impact
evidence.quote: The IPF map (Fig. 7 a) shows that the microstructure is composed of a large number of elongated and distorted grains, with fine recrystallized grains appearing in some regions, indicating that dynamic recovery and localized DRX have occurred under high-temperature shear strain.
At RT, the peak true stress of the alloy is approximately 358 MPa, indicating high yield strength and resistance to deformation.
When the deformation temperature increases to 400°C, the peak true stress of the alloy decreases significantly to 182 MPa, indicating that high temperatures reduce the yield strength of the material.
